data.narrative:
Ultra Robotics is a seed-stage robotics and manufacturing company founded by Jon Miller Schwartz, Max Friefeld, Chetan Parthiban, and Oliver Ortlieb. The company has raised $3M+ to date. The robotics and manufacturing sector comprises a modest peer universe of 9 private companies and 1 public comparable.

Stage-progression analysis is the applicable valuation method given data constraints. Using total capital raised of $3M as a proxy for seed-stage value and applying a 2.5x step-up multiplier typical of seed-to-next-stage progression yields an implied valuation of $8M. The peer-median method is not applicable; while 10 same-sector peers exist, fewer than 3 meet narrow filter criteria (same stage, adjacent stage, or similar valuation tier), making a narrow peer-based approach unreliable. A broader sector median would introduce unacceptable noise.

The triangulated valuation range is $6M (low) to $9M (high), with a median estimate of $8M, based on the single applicable method. Key uncertainties include the true comparability of the limited peer set to Ultra Robotics' specific technology and market position, and the reliability of using total capital raised as a seed-stage valuation proxy absent detailed cap table data. Additional revenue or product-traction data would strengthen conviction in this range.
